title: Let the local knowledge tools read up to 5,000 records
summary: One local capture, which backs the ia kb commands and the MCP door's ia_kb_* tools, keeps its limits of 100 files totalling 8 MiB. A .ia/knowledge.json selection may list up to 5,000 records and 100 resources in 512 KiB (was 1,000 records and 64 KiB; resources stay at 100). A capture without a selection had no record limit; it now refuses past 5,000 records, the limit selections and door scopes share. A record whose body falls past the file or byte limit is reported unavailable and is not served, so a large workspace may need a narrower selection; capturing a whole selection instead refuses when a resource it lists was not read. @inventarch/kb exports these limits as LIMITS.captureRecords, captureFiles, captureBytes and captureSelectionBytes. The door refuses with IA-KB-SCOPE-LIMIT only past 5,000 selectable authored records or 20 MiB of their membership rows (was 1,000 records and 8 MiB); 20 MiB accommodates 5,000 rows at the measured size of about 3.4 kB per row. Packages and legacy envelopes keep their limits: ia kb pack refuses a selection of more than 1,000 records or 64 KiB that the local tools can accept, and now says so in its message. Capture splits and hashes each source file once instead of once per record, and records bound to one document share its text. A local snapshot digest now pins bodies by their hashes, so a citation saved from an earlier version stops resolving until the record is read again. The 1 MiB per-file and 48 KiB response limits are unchanged.
